rounds.proof_sketch: For shape [16,256,256] with dim=1: inner_size=256, block_size=256. Original grid.y = (256+255)/256 = 1. Mutated grid.y = (256+257)/256 = 2. Extra block has inner_idx = 256+threadIdx.x >= 256 = inner_size, so all extra threads hit 'return' guard before any computation or output write.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the ceiling-division formula from (n+block_size-1)/block_size to (n+block_size+1)/block_size. This always produces equal or greater number of blocks, never fewer. The kernel has an explicit guard clause 'if (inner_idx >= inner_size) return;' that filters out all threads in any extra blocks before they perform any computation or write to output. Since the guard is executed before any side-effectful code, the mutation cannot affect program output regardless of input tensor values.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable - the mutation only affects launch configuration by adding extra blocks, and all extra threads are unconditionally filtered by the bounds check guard clause. No input values can change this behavior.
rounds.recommendations: When mutating grid/block dimension calculations, mutations that only INCREASE thread counts (not decrease) combined with proper bounds checking create semantically equivalent mutants. Consider adding mutation testing rules to detect this pattern and mark such mutants as equivalent, or strengthen test coverage by verifying the kernel doesn't access out-of-bounds memory with tools like compute-sanitizer.
